note: A1-A6 applied as a HARD pre-ballot filter over the 80 mined ideas of runs 1-2 (screened 2026-08-19 by 4 gate agents, ideas judged as described in their entries). Four A4 rejections are carried over from run-2 live verification, overriding a run-3 as-described pass. Gate keys: A1-A6 per run-3/PLAN.md; EXCL-1 Clausewright variant; EXCL-2 Ratepin variant; AI-ARBITER = the model would be the source of a decision the customer signs.

rejections.name: MacGuard
rejections.reason: PBM-specific MAC price lists are distributed through payer contracts/portals rather than public machine-readable sources, so the underlying corpus this depends on is paywalled/scrape-hostile; the audit-appeal-generation half also leans on case-specific persuasive drafting with no described degraded mode.

rejections.name: WageBridge
rejections.reason: Core product is a federal/state prevailing-wage rate lookup engine that auto-generates WH-347 certified payroll reports — directly the certified-payroll/Davis-Bacon pattern excluded for this run.

rejections.name: PermitPilot
rejections.reason: The one-liner and why_simple explicitly promise 'filling out the paperwork for you' / 'help filing them' for STR permits — a done-for-you filing service, matching the explicit A2-fail pattern.

rejections.name: ShipCheck
rejections.reason: The deliverable is an LLM prediction of how a subjective human app-store reviewer will rule on ambiguous guideline compliance, not a deterministic computation over settled structured facts — an open-ended generative compliance judgment presented as the product.

rejections.name: WagePilot
rejections.reason: Turns timesheets into WH-347 plus state prevailing-wage certified payroll reports — squarely the excluded certified-payroll/Davis-Bacon pattern.

rejections.name: Tariffly
rejections.reason: Core promise is 'paste a description, get the right HS code' — the AI is the source of the customs classification decision the customer files and pays duty against, not deterministic code applying a known code to a rate table.

rejections.name: StayLegal
rejections.reason: Explicitly described as a 'done-for-you' permit filing service with 'manual concierge filing for the first cohort' — human labor on the seller side fulfilling the core value.

rejections.name: WageLine
rejections.reason: Finds the Davis-Bacon wage determination and craft classification for certified payroll purposes — a direct prevailing-wage/Davis-Bacon lookup pattern excluded for this run.

rejections.name: DutyLens
rejections.reason: The flagship wedge offer is a $1,500 'Tariff Exposure Audit... delivered in 3-5 days,' the classic non-instant human-turnaround signal, and the HS classification itself is an AI-made customs decision the customer signs.

rejections.name: CodeMarshal
rejections.reason: Core product is 'ask any fire-alarm code question, get a cited jurisdiction-specific answer' — an open-ended generative answer to an inherently ambiguous, inspector-dependent compliance question, precisely the excluded pattern.

rejections.name: WageLens
rejections.reason: Explicitly a Davis-Bacon wage-determination and classification lookup that auto-fills WH-347 certified payroll — the excluded certified-payroll/prevailing-wage pattern.

rejections.name: SpaComply
rejections.reason: AI generates binding medical-director/delegation agreements and standing orders in a nuanced, state-varying healthcare-law area (CPOM) with no described human review or degraded mode — the model is effectively the source of a signed legal compliance decision.

rejections.name: Scopewise
rejections.reason: Core value is 'AI chat that answers can I do X in state Y' — an open-ended generative answer to a compliance question is the product itself, not deterministic code against a structured corpus. Underlying corpus (50 states' medical/nursing board rules, CPOM ownership rules) is also scattered across board sites and statute text, a manual-curation A4 risk.

rejections.name: StormClear
rejections.reason: Revenue model explicitly includes a 'rush add-on where the team preps and files the actual state registration/bond paperwork for a flat per-state fee' — a human-fulfilled filing service, not code-only fulfillment.

rejections.name: SpaSentinel
rejections.reason: Sells an 'AI advisor' answering open-ended CPOM/scope-of-practice compliance questions, plus one-time $1,500-$5,000 human-flavored 'compliance gap-analysis/audit reports' — both the open-ended AI legal Q&A and the audit-report deliverable trip the AI-as-engine and A2 rules.

rejections.name: Recoup
rejections.reason: Contingency-fee 'we get your money back from your landlord' service — actual recovery requires disputing with and being paid by a landlord (negotiation/collection), which is not something code alone fulfills; this is a service wrapped in AI, not automated fulfillment of the paid-for outcome.

rejections.name: PackPilot
rejections.reason: Pitch is literally 'we tell you what you owe and file it for you,' plus a paid 'registration concierge' add-on that 'sources and manages the required local authorized representative' — done-for-you human fulfillment of the core paid outcome.

rejections.name: DutyLens
rejections.reason: AI-assisted HTS classification makes the model the source of the tariff code — a legally consequential number the customer relies on for duty payment and CBP compliance — rather than deterministic code computing against a structured corpus.

rejections.name: Solace
rejections.reason: The product's case-checklist value depends on 'state-by-state death-care regulations ... scattered across individual state health department PDFs' — exactly the manual-curation-of-scattered-PDFs pattern the gates fail, wired into the core case workflow, not just an incidental moat note.

rejections.name: DutyDesk
rejections.reason: 'AI copilot that gives small importers the correct tariff (HTS) code' — the AI is the source of a classification decision with direct financial/legal consequences (duty owed, CBP penalty exposure), not a deterministic lookup against a structured corpus.

rejections.name: RateCard
rejections.reason: Benchmark corpus is built by normalizing 'Reddit r/sysadmin and r/CIO renewal-cost threads' and 'LinkedIn we just renewed X for $Y posts' — informal, unverifiable, scattered social data that requires ongoing manual judgment/curation to be trustworthy, not a self-refreshing machine-readable source.

rejections.name: StateSwitch
rejections.reason: Corpus is explicitly 'scattered across individual state board PDFs, one-off press releases' with no central aggregation — the manual-curation-of-scattered-PDFs failure pattern, despite the product itself disclaiming filing services.

rejections.name: PartMatch
rejections.reason: Moat and build plan both rest on 'scraping scattered manufacturer catalogs and spec PDFs' with no common format across verticals — a manually-curated scattered-PDF corpus, not a self-refreshing machine-readable source with staleness detection.

rejections.name: SiteSignal
rejections.reason: Self-described in the one-liner as 'a done-for-you outbound service instead of a raw lead spreadsheet' — the paid deliverable is the outbound execution/booked appointment itself, the exact 'done-for-you' pattern the rules flag as an automatic A2 fail regardless of automation used underneath.

rejections.name: Reinstate
rejections.reason: Amazon/Walmart marketplace account-suspension appeal and Plan-of-Action drafting — a direct Clausewright-variant exclusion for this run.

rejections.name: RefIQ
rejections.reason: Core job stated verbatim: 'ask a compliance question about refrigerants/equipment/code, get a plain-English cited answer' — the textbook open-ended generative compliance answer the AI-as-engine rule prohibits as the product.

rejections.name: Renewly
rejections.reason: Underlying licensing/CE data source is NASCLA's static, infrequently-updated print/PDF guidebooks (28 separate state guidebooks) — a manually-curated scattered-document corpus, not a self-refreshing machine-readable feed; also carries an AI Q&A compliance-answer feature.

rejections.name: ClearHS
rejections.reason: 'Paste a product description or photo ... returns the correct HTS code' — AI is the source of the classification decision underlying the duty rate the customer relies on, the same HTS-classification-as-AI-arbiter pattern as DutyLens/DutyDesk.

rejections.name: FreeTime
rejections.reason: Moat explicitly built from 'each ocean carrier's individually-published D&D tariff and free-time terms (dozens of scattered PDFs/webpages with no common format)' — a manually-curated scattered-PDF corpus rather than a self-refreshing machine-readable source.

rejections.name: BookPulse
rejections.reason: The detection moat is 'chart-of-accounts patterns and common miscategorization signatures' built from QuickBooks Community forum threads, IRS Schedule C mappings, and industry COA templates — scattered human-written sources with no described cron/API refresh or staleness detection, i.e. manual curation to stay correct.

rejections.name: NexusPilot
rejections.reason: The entry's own moat description admits sellers today 'piece together' the 50-state nexus threshold table 'from state DOR websites and blog posts' — no API, no cron, no staleness mechanism described, so the core dataset needs manual curation to stay correct.

rejections.name: TariffPilot
rejections.reason: The product's core deliverable is an LLM 'classification engine' that outputs the exact HS/HTS code and duty rate a customer relies on to pay tariffs and avoid penalties — the model is the source of the classification decision itself, not deterministic code computing against a structured corpus with AI only assisting presentation.

rejections.name: LicenseStack
rejections.reason: Explicitly sells a '$300-$1,500 per state... "we file it for you" service' as a productized upsell alongside the subscription — a literal done-for-you human service, which is the disqualifying phrase the gate names directly.

rejections.name: ScopeIQ
rejections.reason: Core value is described as 'ask which state and which procedures, get back a structured, sourced compliance answer' — an open-ended generative AI answer to a medical scope-of-practice/supervision compliance question, with no deterministic structured-corpus computation described underneath.

rejections.name: PermitPilot
rejections.reason: Depends on 'a structured, continuously scraped and normalized database of thousands of city/county STR ordinances, permit workflows, and renewal deadlines' pulled from planning-department PDFs across thousands of jurisdictions, with no cron cadence or staleness detection described — the classic scattered-PDF manual-curation corpus the gate flags.

rejections.name: StationGrant
rejections.reason: Its own moat description says the winning-narrative knowledge is 'scattered across FEMA PDFs, past award data, and consultants' heads' — explicitly non-machine-readable domain knowledge requiring manual curation, with no refresh cron or staleness mechanism described.

rejections.name: ModWatch
rejections.reason: Core product is 'cron-fed alerts and bid-priced rate cards for federal and state prevailing-wage determinations' built on Davis-Bacon/SCA wage determinations and certified-payroll pain points — a direct match to the Ratepin exclusion (prevailing-wage / Davis-Bacon rate lookup or monitoring).

rejections.name: Bacondesk
rejections.reason: Core product is WH-347 generation plus state e-CPR XML pre-checked against Davis-Bacon wage determinations — squarely certified payroll / prevailing-wage lookup, the explicitly excluded Ratepin category.

rejections.name: Adviserbook
rejections.reason: The paid deliverable is a RAG-generated written annual compliance review and redlined brochure — an open-ended generative answer to 'is this RIA compliant,' not deterministic code computing against a structured corpus with AI only in presentation.

rejections.name: WageLens
rejections.reason: Core product is Davis-Bacon prevailing-wage rate lookup by county/craft plus WH-347 generation — directly the excluded Ratepin category.

rejections.name: UnderwaterRx
rejections.reason: Detects underpaid claims and then generates a downloadable appeal document for the pharmacist to file — an explicit reframe of a prior 'we write your appeals' service into self-serve appeal/plan-of-action drafting, the excluded Clausewright category.

rejections.name: Tierline
rejections.reason: Run-2 verification: the paid deliverable rests on a hand-authored 50-state EPCRA Tier II matrix; EPA itself confirms no consolidated machine-readable source exists. Content-hash crawling detects THAT a page changed, not the new fee/field/format rule. Run-3 screener passed it as described; the run-2 finding is live-verified and prevails.

rejections.name: Trustline
rejections.reason: Run-2 verification: the moat is a 50-state trust/escrow rules matrix with quarterly full re-verification — recurring human work on prose sources. What survives autonomously is a reconciliation feature incumbents already bundle. Run-3 screener passed it as described; the run-2 finding prevails.

rejections.name: NexusPilot
rejections.reason: Run-2 verification (self-admitted in the entry): threshold table extracted from human-readable state DOR pages with no authoritative machine-readable feed for all 46 jurisdictions; the product asserts a dated legal obligation. Shopify ships a free built-in nexus tracker. Run-2 finding prevails.

rejections.name: Tariffgrid
rejections.reason: Run-2 verification: OpenEI URDB freshness is a third party’s human curation programme (Illinois State University), plus standing PUC-docket prose extraction for eligibility clauses; the paid output is a switch recommendation the customer may be unable to execute. Run-2 finding prevails.
